_comment: Canonical confidence-weights config. Read by processor/agent/confidence.py (which nodes.py, run_benchmark_local.py and tune_weights.py all share). Positive signals are combined as a weighted mean over the signals available on a given run; penalty weights are then subtracted outright. A run only opens a PR if the final score >= confidence_threshold. Edit by hand, or regenerate with `python tune_weights.py`.

notes.stack_trace_present: 1.0 for a full traceback with an exception line; 0.8 frames but no 'Traceback' header; 0.4 exception line only; 0.0 nothing (dag6).
notes.line_number_matches_source: 1.0 the failing line of code is where the traceback says it is; 0.6 it exists elsewhere in the file; 0.25 only the function matches; 0.0 the code isn't in this file at all. This is the guard that catches a stale or wrong DAG source being analysed against a fresh log.
notes.known_fix_pattern_match: 1.0 if the exception type is in confidence.KNOWN_FIX_PATTERNS (KeyError, FileNotFoundError, AttributeError, ModuleNotFoundError, ...).
notes.log_completeness: Fraction of six checks: timestamps, level markers, >=4 lines, task_id present, dag_id present, >=200 chars.
notes.history_merge_rate: OPTIONAL. Share of past agent PRs for this dag+task that a human merged. Omitted (not guessed) when there is no history.
notes.retrieval_support: OPTIONAL. min(1, similar prior incidents found / 5).
notes.external_dependency_detected: PENALTY. 1.0 when the failure bottoms out in a third-party call or outage (dag5). Subtracted from the weighted mean so an otherwise-perfect log still lands below threshold, because no change to this repo fixes it.

metadata.source: hand-tuned, validated against config/tuning_fixtures.json (17 rows) with `python tune_weights.py score`
metadata.margin: nearest negative scores 0.614 against a 0.70 threshold; nearest positive scores 1.000
metadata.note: Regenerate with `python tune_weights.py fit --apply` once BigQuery has >=5 human-labeled PR outcomes per class; that overwrites this block with fitted values and their cross-validated accuracy.
